title: Searing Gorge
body: The Searing Gorge was born in fire, when the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros and Blackrock Mountain erupted, scorching the valley to its north black. Today it is a place of ash, lava and ruthless industry. The Dark Irons dug the vast excavation called the Cauldron and filled it with slaves, golems and taskmasters, the Twilight's Hammer keeps a camp in the northwestern hills, and from the cliffs of Thorium Point the Thorium Brotherhood, Dark Iron smiths who broke with their kin, watches it all.

title: Thorium Point
body: Thorium Point clings to the cliffs in the north of the gorge, looking straight down into the Cauldron, the stronghold of the Thorium Brotherhood. Brotherhood lookouts stand watch, a wanted board posts bounties against the Dark Iron crews below, and gryphon and wind rider handlers both keep their mounts here, for the Brotherhood welcomes Alliance and Horde alike.

title: The Cauldron
body: At the heart of the gorge lies the Cauldron, an enormous pit the Dark Iron dwarves carved out of the blackened valley floor in their hunger for ore. Heavy war golems lumber along its ramps, and slave workers toil under the whip, so broken by labor and heat that they turn on would-be rescuers. Four sentry towers guard the rim, and the cutthroat traders of the Undermarket keep a base below under the protection of their Dark Iron partners.

title: Firewatch Ridge
body: The mountains of the northwestern gorge belong to the Twilight's Hammer. Their encampment on Firewatch Ridge is held by fire guards, geomancers and dark shamans, and idolaters carry the cult's symbols of Ragnaros. The cult keeps a grim warning on the ridge: a cage holding the spirit of Zamael Lunthistle, a young night elf who fell in with them, turned back to Elune when a vision woke him, and was put to death as a blasphemer.

title: Stonewrought Pass
body: Stonewrought Pass is a dwarven tunnel joining the Searing Gorge to Loch Modan, the work of Franclorn Forgewright, whose stonewrought method of building also raised the great dam of Loch Modan. For years both ends have been sealed. On the Loch Modan side Mountaineer Pebblebitty keeps the key and turns nearly every traveler away, unless they bring proof of heroics, such as the horn of Margol the Rager, the beast of the gorge's far southeast.

title: Kalaran Windblade
body: Kalaran Windblade keeps a lonely camp on the slopes between Thorium Point and the Cauldron, with no company but his lumbering squire, Maltrake. He tells of a father slain by the filth of the Cauldron and of Stormwind magistrates who would not even admit this corner of the world exists, and swears that riches beyond imagining await anyone who helps him take revenge. When he works his craft he chants in a tongue no one recognizes.

parts.body: His grief was a mask. When the Cauldron's sentry towers burned, a drake of the black dragonflight stood in his place, a servant of the legion of Blackrock: the murdered father was only bait, for no mortal would have helped had Blackrock simply asked.

title: Dorius Stonetender
body: Dorius Stonetender, brother of Curator Thorius of the Hall of Explorers, led an Ironforge excavation at the Grimesilt Dig Site until the Dark Irons took it. Now he lies sprawled among the diggings, groaning that he is bleeding inside and must get back to Ironforge. His one worry, he says, is his team: if anything happened to him, they would be stuck in the Cauldron's mine forever.

parts.body: Short of the gate a Dark Iron marksman brought him down, and he was gone in a cloud of dust, leaving a singed letter for his brother: the Dark Irons held the Suntara stones, and their leader, Lathoric the Black, used them to enslave his team.
sources: quest 3367 description (badly injured, bleeding internally, must get back to Ironforge)

parts.body: Dorius never died. At the dig site he had found the Suntara stones and felt the power of Ragnaros flood into him, and as Lathoric the Black he staged his death to bring rescuers to fetch the last stone he needed.
